edition: Survey IX — consolidated political and civic register
projection: Plate-carree latitude/longitude chart; regional route measurements remain authoritative.

states.name: Veldrassen
states.detail: The crown is a compact among old provinces: its armies and foundries are enormous, but provincial estates bargain over every exceptional levy. Rail contracts and coal exports hold the monarchy together more reliably than court ceremony.
states.industry: Heavy engineering, railway equipment and general manufactures
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Ostrevain
states.detail: Royal commissioners are consolidating an agricultural monarchy into an arsenal state. Landowners favour grain exports; army purchasers want controlled prices and labour for new factories. The resulting dispute reaches from village granaries to the court.
states.industry: Grain distribution, military stores and arsenal production
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Rovessara
states.detail: Merchant councils govern a commercial republic whose banks finance shipping and precision workshops. Foreign clients need its instruments and engines, but the republic depends on open sea lanes and negotiated access to raw materials.
states.industry: Precision instruments, electrical apparatus and overseas commerce
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Brannervaux
states.detail: City charters, landed estates and river authorities divide power in a federation confined to its own basins. Locks, flood protection and water allocation bind members together while producing repeated disputes about who pays upstream and who benefits downstream.
states.industry: Water engineering, agricultural processing and industrial chemistry
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Cervaud
states.detail: A hereditary border duchy buys security by bargaining with Veldrassen and Ostrevain. Its fortified frontier supports a substantial officer class; competing patrons and military purchasing make nominal independence expensive.
states.industry: Frontier logistics, armaments repair and estate agriculture
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Veylac
states.detail: An industrial republic governed through municipal and commercial representation, with a long argument over labour’s place in that settlement. Machine-tool exports pay for essential imports; disputed frontiers consume revenue that towns want spent on housing and power.
states.industry: Metallurgy, machine tools and factory production
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Ossavren successor territories
states.detail: These are the successor territories of a broken crown, not a single nation. Rival palaces, provincial commands and autonomous ports divide its large coal and petroleum resources. Shared roads and kinship survive beneath customs barriers and foreign-backed claimants.
states.industry: Competing provincial administrations, workshops and military supply
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Rovengard
states.detail: The southern valley monarchy holds the largest single government in Morholt. Its crown must secure food routes between farming basins and scattered fortresses; huge forest claims do not translate into a dense tax base or a freely deployable army.
states.industry: Valley agriculture, timber and stronghold supply
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Varnesk
states.detail: Mining councils and foundry proprietors govern a league rather than a royal province. Specialist steel and machinery create wealth, but imported food and negotiated convoy protection limit how far the league can act alone.
states.industry: Ore processing, specialist steels, bearings and durable machinery
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Galdresk
states.detail: A wardenship of chartered orders, estates and civilian towns. Houses of medicine and the older arts preserve useful learning without supplying a large magical army. Obligations of shelter and patrol compete with each district’s limited stores.
states.industry: Field medicine, communications and scholarly traditions
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Halskert
states.detail: River towns and mill proprietors govern a republic tied to seasonal navigation. Its food valleys are valuable to colder neighbours; spring flood control, pilotage and grain contracts dominate political bargaining.
states.industry: River freight, milling and agricultural exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Tervayne
states.detail: A western Vesalian maritime power whose interests face the western ocean. Roughly two thousand kilometres of uplands and intervening governments separate its principal sphere from Veyrasse; it competes with eastern merchants overseas without sharing their local frontier.
states.industry: Maritime freight, ship maintenance and naval supply
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Vardol
states.detail: A northern realm of arsenals, fuel processing and grain districts. Rivalry with Averholt and the bargaining power of military suppliers occupy its government. Road access to Caldrienne exists, but does not turn the eastern Marches into a Vardolian province.
states.industry: Northern arsenals, estate production and military provisioning
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Averholt
states.detail: An inland realm held together by provincial arrangements and productive basins. It contests influence with Vardol and trades through defended passes toward Karsenne. Provincial councils resist campaigns that would strip local defences to fund distant annexations.
states.industry: Basin agriculture, internal trade and provincial engineering
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Serevask Republic
states.detail: The Serevask Republic administers thirteen million people around its surviving civic and industrial districts. It is the remnant of a southern customs federation, never a continental government. Varnelle, Kelbrun and Gavrel administer their own territory, taxation and armed forces. The old federal charter remains an argument over debt and water, not effective authority over them.
states.industry: Federal administration, repair shops and commercial services
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Varnelle
states.detail: The delta authorities gained effective independence from Serevask as rebuilding debts and customs disputes broke the old basin federation. Port and water boards bargain with merchants and troops; river access makes their policies consequential far upstream.
states.industry: Delta freight, customs, filtration and processing trades
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Kelbrun
states.detail: Upriver councils and plantation interests govern separately from Serevask. Rubber chemistry, filtration and agricultural exports bring revenue, while estate labour obligations and downstream water demands provoke persistent disputes.
states.industry: Upriver freight, plantation produce and agricultural machinery
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Gavrel
states.detail: Chartered march houses retain their own levies and recognise only limited common obligations. Their earlier partnership in the southern federation left shared debts and roads, not obedience to Serevask. Small industrial centres depend on negotiated access through their neighbours.
states.industry: March provisioning, rural estates and frontier workshops
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Bellacosta Cantons
states.detail: The cantons grew out of harbour and plantation charters left without a royal guarantor after the Long Culling. Jougrenne convenes the coastal toll assembly; Nantac administers a separate inland land court. Neither can tax the other’s households. Harbour dues fund escorts while plantation owners pay for roads and demand control of the checkpoints. Veldrassen buys tropical produce and timber here, but its purchasing agents face competing canton tariffs rather than a single ministry. Tenant disputes centre on debt and access to cleared farmland; the assembly meets over commercial quarrels, not to command a national army.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Coastal canton assemblies and inland land courts; shared toll negotiations, separate treasuries and troops.

states.name: Cavressa Principalities
states.detail: A chain of small courts and charter towns occupies the southwestern approaches. Collengo’s market charter protects merchants from estate levies, while the lords around Peregia claim payment for escorting their wagons. Winter fodder and access through the uplands matter more than distant dynastic titles. Albaret brokers wool and preserved food between the courts. Marriage contracts frequently change toll rights without moving a border; merchants employ local advocates to interpret them. Southern sea trade offers an alternative to the roads, but only to houses able to finance a shipment.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Independent principalities, free market charters and estate courts; no common sovereign.

states.name: Vaulcerre Basin Leagues
states.detail: Anselleuil’s reservoir command, Jarnan’s commercial council and the estate assemblies around Votane share a drainage basin but not a government. Their water compact survived the destruction of the authority that first imposed it. Gates must open in an agreed order; delaying an upstream release can destroy a downstream planting season. Brannervaux engineers are employed as arbitrators and suspected of favouring their own merchants. Grain barges, mill repair and fertiliser works sustain the towns. Disputes usually begin as inspections, impoundments and unpaid maintenance bills before soldiers become involved.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Three principal water authorities with smaller charter towns; a binding water compact but no unified army.

states.name: Seravelle Littoral
states.detail: Astrellac’s harbour republic and the inland estate courts share the eastern littoral with smaller free ports. Their commercial convention standardises bills of lading but leaves taxes and criminal law local. Shipping families advance money against harvests; rural houses resent foreclosures by creditors who never leave the coast. Rovessaran insurers and instrument makers are influential customers. Port patrols cooperate against raiders, yet seize one another’s cargo when a debt dispute turns political. Hinterland towns depend on export warehouses for salt, tools and credit, which gives the harbours power beyond their formal borders.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Harbour republics and estate courts linked by a maritime commercial convention.

states.name: Haldrevik Concessions
states.detail: Concession houses hold time-limited rights to timber, minerals and fuel rather than sovereignty over every inhabitant. Asanetz keeps the surviving charter archive; Alauvenne houses one of the armed inspection posts. A house can own a railway and still owe rent to the community beneath it. Varnesk firms provide machinery and credit, exchanging technical dependence for preferred ore contracts. Charter renewals provoke strikes, armed intimidation and lawsuits over restoration bonds. Settlements outside a concession bargain for patrols in return for provisions; a company’s withdrawal can be more frightening than its arrival.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Rival concession houses under separate charters; settlement councils retain residence and market law.

states.name: Dreissen Wardholds
states.detail: Dananske, Dreinvar and Ferorvik anchor separate wardholds along the northern approaches. Each warden owes shelter to the villages that provision a fortress, but the obligation is disputed when stores run short. Their annual muster negotiates convoy schedules and exchanges hostages against broken promises; it does not elect a king. Galdresk medical houses maintain small hospices by invitation. Imported grain is strategically more important than ceremonial claims to the iceward interior. Officers measure influence in serviceable engines and winter stores, while civilian assemblies try to keep temporary requisitions from becoming permanent rent.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Independent fortress wardens bound to civilian provisioning charters and a seasonal convoy muster.

states.name: Varneselle Estates
states.detail: The eastern estates descend from competing settlement grants, with Varkessant’s port charter carved out of the landed claims. Estate bailiffs administer courts and patrol obligations; the port elects its own commercial officers. Fishing communities resist attempts to classify their customary shore access as a landlord’s concession. Halskert buys fish and timber and sells grain, giving its merchants leverage in disputes over freight. Family alliances cross estate borders, but succession cases repeatedly fragment holdings. Seasonal workers move between shore crews and inland workshops, carrying news faster than the formal post.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Hereditary estate courts, independent fishing charters and Varkessant’s municipal port government.

states.name: Bressavelle Marches
states.detail: The western marches form a belt of fortified lordships, town liberties and cultivated valleys between larger powers. Temevaux’s command guards a road junction; Malinne’s council controls a different customs district. Neither speaks for the entire belt. Tervayne merchants finance road repairs in exchange for bonded warehouses, while inland patrons subsidise rival toll houses. Small rulers survive by alternating clients and keeping neighbouring courts divided. Textile finishing, estate agriculture and wagon repair support a population far larger than its thinly charted principal towns suggest. A traveller’s permit may be valid for one bridge and useless at the next.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Fortified lordships and town liberties; overlapping foreign patronage, no regional crown.

states.name: Vallessia Cantons
states.detail: Southern market cantons rebuilt around local granaries after the Long Culling. Margeuil’s elected grain board, Darnenne’s military governor and the landed councils around Galigny compete over transport dues. Common measures for grain survived; a common treasury did not. Merchants connect warm lowland crops with cooler interior districts, using brokers who can guarantee passage through several authorities. Kelbrun buyers seek plantation produce and seasonal labour. Municipal councils resist the governors’ claim that every warehouse is a military asset, particularly after poor harvests make requisitions politically dangerous.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Market cantons, landed councils and surviving military governorships; a common weights agreement only.

states.name: Rivessac Coast
states.detail: Saultac is the best-charted inland market in a southeastern coastal region of small port communes and hereditary agricultural districts. The survey’s single principal marker is not its only inhabited place. Pilots’ guilds set practical terms for coastal travel; inland houses control cultivated land and the roads supplying the harbours. Ceralte brokers buy provisions here without governing the coast. Rival communes share storm warnings but guard their harbour soundings. The region’s political disputes concern port fees, seasonal labour and who funds guarded access to inland markets, rather than a single national succession.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.
states.government: Port communes and agricultural districts linked by pilotage agreements; separate administrations.

states.name: Karsenne Compact
states.detail: Drossane hosts common business for autonomous mining councils and fortress districts. The Compact is a federation rather than a unified hereditary realm. Ores, engineering skills and defended approaches sustain its bargaining power, but coastal freight charges consume export income. Valley workshops and cultivated pockets support the upland economy. Veyrasse remains an uneasy defensive partner and vital outlet. A direct railway toward Calvernis is sought, not operating; existing roads do not provide an equivalent bulk-freight service.
states.industry: Mining, military engineering and defended-pass supply
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Duchy of Caldrienne
states.detail: Valdrec houses the ducal administration and principal army depots. Productive valleys support estate agriculture and armament towns; the state fields strong infantry, artillery and a comparatively large armoured force. Ducal supervision is more centralised than in Veyrasse, though estate and arsenal interests still compete for resources. The unresolved Cressault claim strains an armed truce. Northern obligations and imports of Karsenne ore prevent its government from directing every resource against the March.
states.industry: Agriculture, artillery production and armoured-vehicle workshops
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: March of Veyrasse
states.detail: The charter balances the Margrave, landed houses, municipal councils and industrial proprietors. Auvrienne holds the court and government; Serravonne is a secondary port and rail junction. Coastal agriculture and workshops depend on inland ores and imported machinery. Railway unions can disrupt mobilisation, and poorer households bear disproportionate service obligations. Caldrienne remains the principal territorial rival; Karsenne is an essential supplier, while Calvernis and Ceralte provide competing maritime connections. The Margrave commands the standing army and foreign relations, while chartered institutions provide much of the money, manpower and transport. Education and engineering offer advancement through patronage. Railway superintendent Leont Vardesca governs railway affairs and dependants, not Serravonne’s government or army.
states.industry: Railway engineering, port trade and municipal industry
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Calvernis Republic
states.detail: Miravelle is the seat of a republic whose restricted franchise favours shipping, banking and industrial families. Harbour revenues, ship maintenance and manufacturing support convoy escorts, coastal guns, marines and maritime aircraft. Smaller towns supply its commercial ports without erasing rival patronage networks. Veyrasse is a customer and competitor; an alternative outlet for Karsenne could redirect freight and toll income. No agreement has completed that proposed railway.
states.industry: Shipping, banking, shipyards and maritime manufactures
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Ceralte Admiralty
states.detail: Dalmor is the fortified harbour and seat of a hereditary protector, senior naval council and island governors. Fishing, pilotage, convoy services and repair yards sustain the chain, while imported grain remains essential. Torpedo craft, mine warfare and knowledge of difficult waters offset limited land resources. Island communities depend on shipping rather than a mainland-style road network. Treaty cooperation coexists with accusations of privateering; no allegation proves official sponsorship.
states.industry: Coastal trade, fishing, naval maintenance and convoy services
states.population_note: Current population return; ordinary annual trend before exceptional losses and recorded migration.

states.name: Cressault corridor
states.detail: The Cressault corridor is a chain of defended valleys near the Veyrasse–Caldrienne frontier, containing a railway crossing, irrigated farmland and the pumping infrastructure sustaining them. Both states claim it. Some estates owe hereditary obligations to one government while depending on the other for transport and protection. A previous border war ended in an armistice without resolving ownership. Frontier troops exchange occasional fire and patrols sometimes fail to return. Customs inspections and railway delays serve as instruments of pressure. Both governments accuse the other of supporting armed local claimants and interfering with water supplies. Renewed war is feared, but neither government has publicly committed to it. Serravonne is away from this front; its railway carries associated supplies and returning personnel. Its 180,000 residents are counted within Veyrasse for census accounting, without resolving sovereignty.
states.industry: Local agriculture, small workshops and guarded overland exchange
states.population_note: 180,000 residents are included in Veyrasse’s population return, not added to the planetary total. This census attribution does not settle the competing territorial claims.

history: Initial planetary chart. No territorial transfer enacted.
Survey correction: repaired continental outlines, continuous regional detail and principal settlement/transport layer; no territorial transfer.
Survey IV adds district settlements, local roads, branch railways, drainage and fine relief throughout all three continents; existing regional survey and political claims preserved.

Planetary resurvey establishes latitude, oceans, polar regions, islands, tectonic provinces, drainage and climatic belts. Local railway measurements and Eastern Marches records retained; no in-story territorial transfer.
Survey VI: southern polar bedrock, irregular island shores, continuous mountain relief, upland drainage and connected continental road systems. Regional measurements retained.

history.change: Eastern Marches district settlements, roads and expanded civic records. Original places, measured journeys and political/census totals preserved.

Removed 59 over-sampled invented district markers and their redundant links; retained the original seven centres and ten separated district centres. Added independent northern, southern and western overland gateways. No population loss, migration, territorial change or elapsed story time.

boundary_note: Generalised irregular political boundaries; shared edge vertices preserved. No territorial change.

sites.name: Cavrelisse
sites.detail: The highland court and provincial assembly occupy terraces above government stores and crowded service wards. Delegations bargain over coal duties and military levies here; grain arrives from lower agricultural districts, making rail interruptions politically dangerous. The surrounding survey records alpine rock and meadow, at approximately 3,800 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Coniocce (rail), Moncraux (road), Veniossia (road), Mondessore (rail), Molessac (rail).

sites.name: Mondessore
sites.detail: Locomotive erecting shops, boiler works and a large repair labour force anchor this manufacturing city. Suppliers compete for crown contracts, while skilled workers can halt deliveries by withholding overtime. Foundry quarters and wealthier engineers’ streets have markedly different air and housing. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 2,200 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Veraliana (road), Baleanne (rail), Patora (road), Vamatto (rail), Nimigia (road), Molessac (rail), Cavrelisse (rail).

sites.name: Orsevigne
sites.detail: The royal ministries direct grain procurement and arsenal expansion from an old estate capital. Land agents, officers and provincial petitioners compete for access to the same clerks. Wholesale grain prices matter here almost as much as court appointments. The surrounding survey records wet tropical forest, at approximately 250 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Freissasco (road), Souissetta (road), Tarielle (road), Balbraux (rail), Covetto (road), Tessarone (rail), Charvessant (rail), Astrellac (rail), Vezarolle (rail).

sites.name: Tessarone
sites.detail: New arsenal districts have grown around older metalworking wards. Long municipal queues for housing sit beside ambitious factory compounds; military contracts bring wages and tighter supervision. Agricultural estates still own much of the surrounding land. The surrounding survey records wet tropical forest, at approximately 50 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Ardelleuil (rail), Faugrera (rail), Chabran (road), Orsevigne (rail), Astrellac (rail).

sites.name: Bellacenne
sites.detail: Commercial councils, bank offices and technical institutes crowd the republican capital. Credit and shipping insurance bring foreign clients into its cafés; labour and merchant representatives dispute who benefits from its precision industries. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 950 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Ausera (road), Gerino (road), Jauviglio (rail), Elnegia (rail), Elnegia (road), Pellavore (rail), Avellori (rail).

sites.name: Avellori
sites.detail: Instrument shops and electrical works depend on a network of small specialist suppliers. Apprentices move between family firms and larger factories; a failed glass, copper or bearing delivery can stop an expensive final assembly far away. The surrounding survey records wet tropical forest, at approximately 50 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Alronecce (road), Ririllo (road), Pervac (rail), Pellavore (rail), Bellacenne (rail).

sites.name: Rivessole
sites.detail: Federal delegates negotiate flood works and apportioned revenue in a city of grain brokers and water engineers. Upstream and downstream members can agree that a reservoir is necessary while spending years disputing its price. The surrounding survey records dry grassland and steppe, at approximately 550 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Zubier (rail), Zubier (road), Orlacento (road), Poleelle (road), Abrescois (rail), Molessac (rail), Alescogne (rail).

sites.name: Molessac
sites.detail: Food processing, chemical works and pumping-equipment yards link the city to the federation’s farms. Effluent and irrigation allocations are recurring public disputes; factory employment competes with the needs of cultivated districts. The surrounding survey records desert and rain-shadow scrub, at approximately 250 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Quissac (road), Mevatto (rail), Maubetta (road), Argellonne (road), Mondessore (rail), Rivessole (rail), Cavrelisse (rail).

sites.name: Charvessant
sites.detail: The ducal household shares the capital with a large military bureaucracy and competing foreign purchasing missions. Tailors, armourers and boarding houses thrive on uniforms; local merchants dislike the uncertainty created by rival patrons. The surrounding survey records wet tropical forest, at approximately 600 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Gimasinio (rail), Moisset (road), Faragia (road), Boneno (road), Bamianne (road), Vezarolle (rail), Orsevigne (rail).

sites.name: Vezarolle
sites.detail: Repair yards and military stores support the border army. Much work is maintenance rather than invention, and old equipment accumulates beside replacement parts from incompatible suppliers. Civilian workshops compete with the garrison for fuel. The surrounding survey records wet tropical forest, at approximately 50 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Bavana (road), Gannac (rail), Fesane (rail), Faissier (road), Tolalotto (road), Charvessant (rail), Orsevigne (rail).

sites.name: Alescogne
sites.detail: Municipal delegates and commercial associations conduct the republic’s business amid a strong print and café culture. Machine-tool exporters favour open borders; veterans and frontier proprietors press for protection and armament. The surrounding survey records alpine rock and meadow, at approximately 2,600 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Dasegia (road), Vachetta (road), Fenaragia (road), Condrano (road), Botalatto (road), Bellorante (rail), Rionvesse (rail), Rivessole (rail), Ossendrienne (rail).

sites.name: Bellorante
sites.detail: A manufacturing city of casting shops, cutting tools and specialist repair firms. Cooperative dining rooms and private canteens serve neighbouring shifts. Skilled tradespeople wield influence, but export downturns spread quickly into household debt. The surrounding survey records boreal forest and tundra, at approximately 1,800 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Rarino (rail), Chassento (road), Botalatto (rail), Royatengo (rail), Javeuil (road), Courvetta (road), Rionvesse (rail), Alescogne (rail).

sites.name: Ossendrienne
sites.detail: One claimant maintains a palace, tax offices and military stores here; the city does not rule the whole former crown. Diplomats from larger neighbours support competing clients, and civil servants still file claims to revenue their government cannot collect. The surrounding survey records desert and rain-shadow scrub, at approximately 550 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Ambran (rail), Voterera (rail), Acquesset (rail), Nyssaux (road), Tressavio (rail), Alescogne (rail).

sites.name: Tressavio
sites.detail: Industrial proprietors balance contracts from rival successor authorities. Coal, oil products and machinery cross customs barriers under negotiated permits; interrupted payments can leave valuable plant idle without any physical damage. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 50 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Nantaux (road), Tatogia (rail), Tesivra (road), Ossendrienne (rail), Rionvesse (rail).

sites.name: Arvendal
sites.detail: The crown’s offices distribute supplies and patrol obligations among valley governors. Seasonal petitioners arrive with requests for bridges, grain and escorts. A substantial service population depends on food moving out of the monarchy’s sheltered farming districts. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 50 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Cusssk (road), Derisnov (rail), Eslovanne (rail), Lannard (road), Nerinetz (road), Halsavik (rail).

sites.name: Eslovanne
sites.detail: Timber processing and durable machinery workshops serve dispersed strongholds. Winter stores occupy conspicuous compounds; workers’ families preserve fish and roots long before snowfall. Delayed freight can matter more than a distant court proclamation. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 200 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Garenrek (road), Derisnov (road), Arvendal (rail), Nerinetz (road), Nasinuven (road), Cusssk (road), Halsavik (rail), Corsavik (rail).

sites.name: Corsavik
sites.detail: League councils meet beside commodity offices where ore grades and furnace orders are negotiated. Mine owners and organised trades disagree over working conditions, yet share an interest in protecting imported food and transport. The surrounding survey records boreal forest and tundra, at approximately 2,050 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Risurin (rail), Alenvik (road), Peraask (road), Norsavia (rail), Eslovanne (rail).

sites.name: Norsavia
sites.detail: Specialist steel and bearing works serve customers beyond Morholt. Heat, reliable power and skilled inspection are essential; an expensive export industry exists beside crowded workers’ housing and tightly rationed winter supplies. The surrounding survey records boreal forest and tundra, at approximately 850 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Derevnov (road), Hasenovre (road), Risurin (road), Corsavik (rail).

sites.name: Grevallier
sites.detail: The wardens’ council, civilian petition offices and medical houses maintain an uneasy balance of authority. Archives preserve the older arts, but most residents work in ordinary services and trades. Patronage determines access to the rare capable teachers. The surrounding survey records glacier and polar ice, at approximately 2,350 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Beravvik (rail), Ventsk (road), Durbdal (road), Deraevlen (road), Verniselle (rail), Tresselund (rail), Varkessant (rail).

sites.name: Verniselle
sites.detail: Workshop courtyards produce communications and field-hospital equipment. Suppliers work beside order-sponsored infirmaries; technical apprentices and medical trainees meet in inexpensive boarding houses. Winter convoys govern the availability of specialised materials. The surrounding survey records boreal forest and tundra, at approximately 1,000 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Torevden (road), Lesiarske (road), Beranske (road), Grevallier (rail), Tresselund (rail).

sites.name: Orsendal
sites.detail: Mill owners, elected civic delegates and navigation interests bargain over the republic’s seasonal revenues. Warehousing and food distribution dominate its commercial life; uncertainty over a coming thaw can unsettle credit before any flood occurs. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 250 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Megndal (rail), Eserdal (rail), Segnard (rail), Seleruske (road), Tresselund (rail).

sites.name: Tresselund
sites.detail: Grain processing and repair trades supply river districts and colder neighbours. The mills’ demand for transport places workers, carriers and farmers in close dependence. Household smokehouses and communal ovens remain important beside industrial facilities. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 600 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Aloach (road), Vedsk (rail), Segnard (road), Megndal (road), Orsendal (rail), Verniselle (rail), Grevallier (rail).

sites.name: Tervessac
sites.detail: The maritime government’s banks and shipping offices arrange western trade and convoy protection. Its wealthy households look overseas for partners. Eastern Vesalian affairs arrive as commercial intelligence rather than daily local politics. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 1,100 metres elevation. sites.name: Serravonne
sites.detail: A fortified secondary port and railway junction in the March of Veyrasse on eastern Vesalius, reached by the hillside railway. Cleared ground, drainage works and guarded rail access protect its industrial yards. Dark stone and concrete walls overlook crowded roofs, chimneys and harbour lights. The station contains a maintenance room with benches, work clothing, a stove, a ledger desk and a wall telephone. Galahad lived under Corva’s care from his first night until leaving for Auvrienne, sleeping in an alcove adjoining the kitchen. It remains his family home; his current lodging is at the Collegium. Superintendent Leont Vardesca has authorised his meals and necessary clothing on the station account. A storeroom, washroom and workshop support the station’s daily work. The alcove bed has been lengthened as Galahad grows. During the year, a hunter strike on a pumping installation farther along the line disrupted deliveries and made emergency repairs the workshop’s priority.

sites.name: Auvrienne
sites.detail: Auvrienne, Veyrasse’s capital, rises in terraces above an extensive railway basin. Freight warehouses, cranes and furnace-lit workshops occupy the lower city. Retaining walls support roads climbing toward pale government buildings with steep roofs and narrow towers. Gun positions overlook the railway cutting. Electric trams serve the streets. Near the freight-yard exit stand a booking office and a glass-covered street plan; farther uphill are an iron-railed monument and an illuminated inn. A bookseller occupies a nearer shopfront. The Auvrienne Collegium of Civil Engineering occupies a broad terrace behind iron railings, with a grey-stone main building, courtyard and teaching workshops. Odran Savel serves as Examiner in Mechanics and sponsors Galahad’s work. Following completion of all curricula, Galahad remains a resident scholar and occasional teacher, receiving a stipend alongside lodging and meals. The library has been read twice; specialised collections and laboratories retain separate access arrangements. Institutional and professional connections support his expanding research. The Margrave resides and governs in a fortified palace and government precinct on Auvrienne’s upper terraces, overlooking the city and railway basin. The household occupies the palace; adjoining buildings contain the chancery, treasury and military secretariat. Court and state policy are centred there, while municipal offices administer the city. The Collegium maintains connections through engineering work and patronage.

sites.name: Salvestre
sites.detail: A northern Veyrasse market borough where frontier carriers buy provisions and arrange freight onward. Customs uncertainty brings business to storekeepers but makes credit expensive. Its fields and workshops belong to several proprietors whose loyalties are not identical. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 150 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Cressault crossing (road), Corteuil (road), Auvrienne (road), Maresse (road).

sites.name: Maresse
sites.detail: An escarpment-side Veyrasse service town handling equipment repairs and provisions for inland traffic. Carriers debate coastward freight charges over bean stew; workshop owners depend on both agricultural customers and passing mineral consignments. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 150 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Auvrienne (road), Salvestre (road).

sites.name: Corteuil
sites.detail: A western Caldrienne district centre where farm produce meets traffic from the escarpment. Inns, veterinary yards and repair trades support carriers. Military purchasing competes with local households for fodder and cartage. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 150 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Salvestre (road), Valdrec (road), Cervasca (road).

sites.name: Rocoise
sites.detail: A northern Caldrienne road town serving the approaches toward Vardol. Road maintenance, guarded stores and customs business support its market. Northern trade gives residents interests distinct from officials chiefly concerned with Cressault. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 0 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Valdrec (road), Cervasca (road).

sites.name: Cervasca
sites.detail: An inland Caldrienne borough where estate collection yards and local workshops serve scattered defended farms. Land agents and market traders dispute weights and charges. Its road links matter more to daily life than the distant coastal fleet. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 0 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Corteuil (road), Rocoise (road).

sites.name: Lucaune
sites.detail: A southern Karsenne district centre supplying road traffic toward Calvernis. Dairy produce, repair shops and carrier lodgings support its market. Residents favour better southern freight access, though roads cannot match a completed mineral railway’s capacity. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 0 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Lucegno (road), Drossane (road), Maroise (road).

sites.name: Maroise
sites.detail: A northern compact borough serving small workings and defended upland households. Its council balances ore contracts against the cost of maintaining exposed roads. Salt, flour and replacement machinery must arrive from beyond the local valleys. The surrounding survey records temperate woodland and farmland, at approximately 150 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Drossane (road), Lucaune (road).

sites.name: Arvegno
sites.detail: An inland Calvernian borough with agricultural markets and equipment repair yards. Carriers bring goods toward the republican coast and neighbouring uplands. Local proprietors want transport improvements without accepting every levy demanded by maritime financiers. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 0 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Lucegno (road), Serrenne (road).

sites.name: Serrenne
sites.detail: A southern Calvernian district centre where food merchants, repair trades and travellers share crowded market streets. Road traffic toward the southern basins spreads both customs disputes and new cooking habits. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 100 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Miravelle (road), Arvegno (road), Lucegno (road).

sites.name: Lucegno
sites.detail: A northern Calvernian road town supplying warehouses and carriers near the Karsenne approaches. Merchants see potential in the proposed railway, but current livelihoods depend on the existing roads and ordinary coastal contracts. The surrounding survey records seasonal woodland and savanna, at approximately 0 metres elevation. Direct transport connections: Lucaune (road), Arvegno (road), Serrenne (road).

geology.model: Present-day tectonic provinces with older inherited fold belts.

planet.reference: Temperate reference meridian; longitude is a cartographic convention.
planet.polar_climate: Both polar bedrock masses carry ice sheets; surrounding polar seas have shelf and seasonal sea ice. Cold marine influence moderates into northern Morholt and Vesalian latitudes, with a wide southern ocean separating Otranto from Austral Land.

regional_record.title: Eastern Vesalius
regional_record.epoch: Planetfall + one standard year and eight days

coordinate_system.projection: Local planar regional grid; campaign travel distances approximate

regional_record.note: 1,200 × 1,600 km regional extract. Borders show territorial claims, not continuous occupation. Caldrienne and Calvernis extend beyond the sheet.

regions.name: Karsenne Compact
regions.detail: Inland fortress and mining federation. Mountain troops, engineers and defended passes. Essential supplier and uneasy partner of Veyrasse; disputes coastal freight charges and seeks a route through Calvernis.

regions.name: Duchy of Caldrienne
regions.detail: Northern hereditary state. Strong infantry, artillery and the region’s largest tank concentration. Veyrasse’s principal territorial rival; commerce continues under an armed truce.

regions.name: March of Veyrasse
regions.detail: Galahad’s home state. A hereditary margrave shares practical power with houses, councils and industrial patrons. Serravonne is a secondary port and railway junction. Standing army, territorial garrisons and household troops defend the March.

regions.name: Calvernis Republic
regions.detail: Southern commercial republic dominated by shipping, banking and industrial families. Convoy escorts, coastal guns, marines and maritime aircraft. Veyrasse’s trading partner and competitor; potential outlet for Karsenne’s alternative export route.

regions.name: Ceralte Admiralty
regions.detail: Offshore island power ruled by a protector and naval council. Experienced crews, torpedo craft and minelaying. Treaty partner against piracy and hunters; allegations of sheltering privateers remain unproven.

regions.name: Cressault corridor
regions.detail: Disputed by Veyrasse and Caldrienne. Defended valleys, a railway crossing, farmland and pumping infrastructure. An armistice ended the previous war without settling ownership. Occasional frontier fire and mutual accusations continue; renewed war is not declared.

local_approach.note: Upland branch from Serravonne; omitted at regional scale.

history.date: Planetfall + one standard year and eight days
history.description: Initial regional disposition; Cressault remains disputed. No territorial change recorded.

history.date: Planetfall + one standard year and eight days
history.description: Regional survey adds measured geography and transport distances; no territorial transfer.

demography.epoch: Ten months and eleven days after Collegium enrolment — evening

history.event: Survey VII: additional Eastern Marches settlements identified within existing census returns; no elapsed time or population growth applied.

rules.annual_step: Next population = present population + rounded births - rounded ordinary deaths + recorded net migration + exceptional event adjustments.
rules.ordinary_mortality: Includes ordinary disease, engineered-wildlife hazards and recurrent low-level conflict. Named disasters and exceptional attacks are separate adjustments, applied once.
rules.migration: Internal migration must debit an origin and credit a destination by the same number.
rules.subsets: City populations and Cressault are included within the listed census groups. No double counting.
rules.time: Advance only with elapsed story time; opening the phone app never advances the census.
rules.review: Rates are current annual trends, reviewed when conditions change; they are not an automatic centuries-long forecast.

polar_landmasses.name: Austral Land
polar_landmasses.detail: Ice-covered southern continental bedrock; no permanent human settlement recorded.

polar_landmasses.name: Boreal Land
polar_landmasses.detail: Northern polar bedrock beneath an ice sheet; fringing shelves face the North Polar Sea.

climate_model: Latitude, elevation, moisture, prevailing winds, rain shadows and cold high-latitude marine influence. Polar ice cover is separate from bedrock. Qualitative climatic reconstruction, not an atmospheric circulation simulation.
